why: The answer depends on soil micro-organisms being the major sink that oxidises atmospheric carbon monoxide, an environmental-chemistry fact.
note: SUBJECT MISASSIGNMENT, not a taxonomy gap. This is a Chemistry question, but the item is labelled subject="Biology" and so carries the closed list of 32 Biology chapters; the correct chapter cannot be in it. Expected chapter: Environmental Chemistry (absent from the Chemistry list too). Root cause is recorded in the item's own source record papers_v2/papers/2017_C.json, which says subject_from = "position (no heading governs this question; the 179-question layout was assumed)". The assumed layout (Physics 1-45, Chemistry 46-90, Biology 91-180) does not match 2017_C, whose actual order is Biology q1-q90, Physics q91-q135, Chemistry q136-q180. Every question in this paper is therefore handed the wrong subject's chapter list, and no honest code exists in the supplied list. Fix the subject assignment for 2017_C and re-run QCHAP rather than filing these anywhere. Separately, even the correct Chemistry list has no 'Environmental Chemistry' chapter, so this item is BOTH misrouted and a real taxonomy gap.
